growth_stages.name: Maturity & Ripening
growth_stages.description: Capsules ripen from the bottom of the plant upward. Sesame is notoriously prone to seed loss from shattering once capsules dry and pop open, timing the cut correctly matters more here than for most crops.

operations.name: Land Clearing
operations.description: Removal of vegetation/debris from the plot.

operations.name: Land Preparation
operations.description: Work soil to a fine tilth and level well, sesame's tiny seed demands a firm, fine, weed-free seedbed for even, shallow sowing.

operations.name: Planting
operations.description: Broadcast thinly or drill in 45-60cm rows; sow shallow, 1-2cm deep. Direct seeded, no nursery stage.

operations.name: Thinning
operations.description: Thinning dense stands, which otherwise suppress capsule development.

operations.name: Fertilizer (NPK/Urea, early)
operations.description: Applied early, sesame's weak root system cannot make use of late fertilizer once flowering starts.

operations.name: Pest & Disease Scouting/Control
operations.description: No specific pest or disease was named for sesame in the source document's GAP process flow, unlike maize, tomato, or rice. This is a genuine gap, not an assumption that sesame has no pest or disease pressure, flagged for a dedicated follow-up sourcing pass.

operations.name: Harvest (Cutting)
operations.description: Cut when the lowest capsules turn yellow/brown but before they pop open. Timing is unusually consequential for this crop: a harvest even a few days late can shed roughly half the yield to the soil through shattering.

operations.name: Post-Harvest Handling (Curing & Threshing)
operations.description: Cut plants are stooked/bundled upright to cure, then threshed gently onto a tarpaulin to minimize further shatter loss.

validation_rules.condition: Land preparation cannot be logged before land clearing. Interval itself not stated in the source document's GAP flow for sesame specifically, carried over as a reasonable default consistent with other crop files. Flagged for review.
validation_rules.source: AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset, Agrolinking Solutions Ltd., July 2026 (GAP process structure); specific 30-day interval not stated in the sesame section itself

validation_rules.condition: Planting cannot occur before land preparation. Interval itself not explicitly stated for sesame in the source document, carried over as a reasonable default. Flagged for review.
validation_rules.source: AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset, Agrolinking Solutions Ltd., July 2026 (GAP process structure); specific 14-day interval not stated in the sesame section itself

validation_rules.condition: Thinning should be done by 21 days after planting, dense stands suppress capsule development. The source frames this as 'soft warning if not logged' by that point, an absence-based check this schema cannot directly represent (validation_rules only fire when an operation IS submitted). What this rule CAN enforce: if thinning IS logged, flag it as late when it happens after 21 days.
validation_rules.source: AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset, Agrolinking Solutions Ltd., July 2026

validation_rules.condition: Fertilizer should be applied early; flagged if logged after 30 days after planting. See sesame_r4_floor for the hard block at 45 days.
validation_rules.source: AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset, Agrolinking Solutions Ltd., July 2026

validation_rules.condition: Hard block if fertilizer is logged after 45 days after planting, sesame's weak root system cannot use late fertilizer once flowering starts.
validation_rules.source: AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset, Agrolinking Solutions Ltd., July 2026

validation_rules.condition: Harvest cannot be logged before 75 days after planting. No stated upper hard block, but see sesame_r5b: a harvest logged after 115 days is flagged, since by that point roughly half the yield can already have shattered onto the soil.
validation_rules.source: AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset, Agrolinking Solutions Ltd., July 2026

validation_rules.condition: 85-115 days after planting is the typical cutting window. Harvest logged inside the hard block range (75+ days) but outside this window is flagged, either too early (risk of immature capsules) or too late (a 120-day harvest can shed roughly half the yield to shattering).
validation_rules.source: AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset, Agrolinking Solutions Ltd., July 2026

validation_rules.condition: Global rule: no operation may be logged with a date earlier than the previous operation's logged date for the same farm/cycle (no backdating that would reorder the sequence).

soil_requirements.drainage: not sourced from the master ruleset's GAP process flow, which focuses on seedbed fineness (fine, weed-free tilth) rather than soil type or pH. pH, texture, and nitrogen_needs fields deliberately omitted rather than guessed at (nitrogen_needs specifically must be one of low/medium/high per the schema, and we don't have a sourced basis to pick one). Flagged as a real gap needing a dedicated sourcing pass.

weather_preferences.notes: Not sourced from the master ruleset's GAP process flow, which focuses on process timing rather than climate requirements. Rainfall and temperature fields deliberately omitted rather than guessed at. The source does note sesame is grown in the Middle Belt and North. Flagged as a real gap needing a dedicated sourcing pass.

yield_model.expected_yield_per_hectare: 0.2 - 0.8 (standard smallholder range), up to 1.0+ with GAP management
yield_model.notes: Derived from the yield_validation tiers below, which are directly sourced, rather than from a separately stated yield figure in the source document.

tiers.message: A reported yield of 0 t/ha must be logged as a Disaster/Loss Event, not a harvest record.
Crop failure -- heavy rain at flowering, poor weeding, or extreme shatter.

yield_validation.source: AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset, Agrolinking Solutions Ltd., July 2026. NOTE: the source table for sesame did not include an explicit 0 t/ha row (unlike maize, rice, and tomato, which did). The equals_zero tier here is an INFERENCE, added for consistency and because a genuine 0-yield report is a plausible real input that the system needs to handle, not a directly sourced figure for this specific crop. Same GPS-anchored-area caveat as the other crops applies. BUGFIX (v1.1.0): the Pass tier's originally-stated ceiling (0.8 t/ha) and the Soft Warning tier's stated floor (>1.0 t/ha) left 0.8-1.0 t/ha covered by neither -- a real, previously-undetected gap that would have made engine.yield_validator.validate_yield() raise a ValueError for a plausible real harvest (e.g. 0.9 t/ha) instead of returning a result. Caught by a new automated test (test_no_yield_validation_gaps_in_plausible_range in tests/test_yield_validator.py), added specifically because every prior gap found in this knowledge base (yam.json, groundnut.json, pepper.json, onion.json, oil_palm.json, rubber.json, coffee.json, cotton.json) had only ever been caught by a manual one-off script re-run by hand per file, not by anything that ran automatically across every crop -- including this pre-existing one, which predates that whole batch. Resolved the same way as this knowledge base's other gap fixes: extended the Pass tier's ceiling from 0.8 to 1.0 to meet the warning tier's floor exactly.

version_history.changed_by: AgTrail Knowledge Base - sixth crop template, first sourced directly from the AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset
version_history.summary: First crop built from the master ruleset rather than general web research, and the first of the ruleset's actual High priority crops (Cocoa was already built before the ruleset arrived; Sesame, Ginger, Cashew, and Hibiscus are the remaining High priority crops). Two real gaps carried forward honestly rather than filled with guesses: the source document's GAP process flow does not name any specific pest or disease for sesame (unlike maize, tomato, and rice, which all had named threats), and does not give soil pH or climate requirements, focusing instead on process timing. Two rules (sesame_r1, sesame_r2, land clearing and planting timing) reuse defaults from other crop files since the source doesn't state sesame-specific intervals for those particular steps. The yield_validation equals_zero tier was inferred rather than directly sourced, since the source table for sesame skipped that row. Not yet reviewed beyond this first pass.
version_history.source: AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset, Agrolinking Solutions Ltd., July 2026

version_history.changed_by: AgTrail Knowledge Base - bugfix via new automated yield-gap-detection test
version_history.summary: Fixed a genuine, previously-undetected gap in yield_validation.tiers: 0.8-1.0 t/ha was covered by neither the Pass tier (stated ceiling 0.8) nor the next Soft Warning tier (stated floor >1.0), which would have made validate_yield() raise instead of returning a result for a real farmer reporting e.g. 0.9 t/ha. This predates and is unrelated to the Medium-priority crop batch (yam/groundnut/pepper/onion/oil_palm/rubber/coffee/cotton) -- it was caught only because a new automated test was added specifically because those crops' gaps had all previously been found by one-off manual scripts, not anything that ran for every crop automatically. See yield_validation.source for the fix.

version_history.changed_by: AgTrail Knowledge Base - platform bugfix, land-prep sequencing gate
version_history.summary: Bumped min_days_after_dependency from 0 to 1 on sesame_r1, sesame_r2, in response to a real bug the user found while using the platform: land preparation could be logged and the very next dependent stage logged on the SAME DAY, with no gap enforced at all, even though the workflow conceptually expects one stage to be completed/settled before the next begins. min=0 technically meant '0 or more days later', which permitted same-day submissions. This is a data-authoring fix (a deliberate rule-value choice), not an engine bug -- the engine was correctly enforcing exactly what the rule said, the rule just said something too permissive. No maximum-day-window or severity changed, and no other rule in this file was touched.
